item.text: I found one subtle point that matters for exact output: the Python program prints the dumper result with an extra newline, so the final stream ends with two `\n` characters for most non-empty block outputs. I’m matching that explicitly rather than relying on Node defaults.

item.text: I found one CLI mismatch: `argparse` accepts a single `--a` value that starts with `- ` when it’s clearly not an option token, and my first pass rejected it. I’m narrowing the option-detection rule so YAML documents like `- 1\n- two` pass correctly while real option-shaped tokens still fail the same way.

item.text:
Created the ESM migration under `/output`.

Library files:
- [args.mjs](/output/lib/cli/args.mjs)
- [nodes.mjs](/output/lib/yaml/nodes.mjs)
- [text.mjs](/output/lib/yaml/text.mjs)
- [scalars.mjs](/output/lib/yaml/scalars.mjs)
- [parser.mjs](/output/lib/yaml/parser.mjs)
- [dumper.mjs](/output/lib/yaml/dumper.mjs)

Entry file:
- [test13.mjs](/output/test13.mjs)

The implementation is pure `.mjs` ESM, uses only local imports, manually parses `process.argv`, and reimplements the required `yaml.safe_load` plus `yaml.dump(..., default_style='"')` behavior in Node without npm dependencies.

I verified it against `/workspace/dataset/test13_executable` on the provided samples and additional cases covering `--a=value`, empty input, flow collections, timestamps, explicit tags, comments, block scalars, nested sequences, and byte-level output for representative cases.
